newsitem.title: USA: U.S. power output rises 0.7 pct vs. year ago--EEI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. power output rises 0.7 pct vs. year ago--EEI.

text.p: Electricity deliveries in the continental U.S. totaled 55,754 gigawatt hours (GWh) for the week ended April 5, up 0.7 percent from the same period in 1996, the Edison Electric Institute (EEI) said Tuesday.
The amount of weekly power supplied to the Pacific Southwest area showed the largest year-to-year increase, up 4.3 percent to 4,495 GWh, EEI said.
The West Central region experienced the largest decrease in power output, falling 1.2 percent from the corresponding period a year earlier to 4,092 GWh.
Year-to-date domestic power production for the first 14 weeks of 1997 totaled 870,801 GWh, up 0.1 percent from the same period in 1996, EEI said.
